If the highest mountains above sea level today (9 km’s for Mount Everest) were covered by water that rose seven meters (or 15 cubits) higher than those mountains during the Flood, the world would have been covered with water forever, because the continents would have been too deep under the water. The mountains had to have been lower than they are today and there had to have been geological sinking and upheavals to make room for all that water — and for us.

qa.question: Why are the ocean basins so deep today?
qa.answer: Because they now needed to serve as reservoirs for the massive amounts of water from the Flood. This means that the water from the Biblical Flood can still be seen today, because it is still being stored in the ocean!

qa.question: How much of the earth surface is covered by water today?
How were the canyons formed?
qa.answer: This global water mass eventually flattened the pre-Flood hills and mountains through erosion. After the floodwater had covered the highest mountains, God spoke and the waters ‘hastened away’. This means that the enormous and fast-moving body of water would have caused extensive erosion when tonnes of soil were washed from the continents into the sea, leaving behind holes, trenches, ravines and even canyons. In this way, extensive erosion contributed to the basic formation of our landscapes today. So Canyons such as these were formed very rapidly, not slowly!

qa.question: Do we have examples today of canyons/valleys that formed rapidly?
qa.answer: Little Grand Canyon = 1 day. Burlingame Canyon (USA) = Less than 6 days. Steppe Canyon, etc

qa.question: What is the ‘recipe’ required for rapid canyon formation?
qa.answer: A LOT of water and a little bit of time.

qa.question: How does volcanic eruptions affect climatic conditions?
qa.answer: Volcanic eruptions causes pollutants such as dust and ash to be shot up right into the stratosphere (between 16-48 km’s high) where they remain for several years. The presence of massive amounts of these pollutants in the stratosphere can reduce sun radiation by as much as 20% which causes a definite reduction in temperature.

qa.question: How did volcanic eruptions affect the climate during the Flood?
qa.answer: There are literally thousands of extinct volcanoes around the world and this includes volcanoes under the sea. Their location in the geologic column indicate that they were still active towards the end of the Flood and for a period thereafter while the floodwater receded. Thousands of volcanoes erupted at the same time during the Flood. The huge amounts of dust and ash particles shooting into the stratosphere must have drastically influenced the climatic conditions. The combination of dust, ash and smoke in the stratosphere would have darkened the sky considerably preventing the sun’s rays from reaching the earth and warming it, which is why the landmass must have cooled very rapidly.

qa.question: Why were the oceans warmer after the Flood than before?
qa.answer: When the fountains of the deep broke open at the beginning of the Flood, causing the oceanic ridges to tear open, super hot lava pushed up through these ridges to form a brand new sizzling hot seafloor. This hot new seafloor caused the ocean waters to be considerably warmer after the Flood than before.

qa.question: What happens when the oceans are so warm?
qa.answer: Warm oceans cause an increase in evaporation, and because of this a large amount of warm moisture and clouds are formed in the air. When warm air moves over a cold landmass, the warm air cools rapidly.

qa.question: Why were the landmasses cold after the Flood?
qa.answer: Volcanic dust and ash blocked out the sun’s rays preventing it from warming the landmass. The warm oceans would have caused an increase in moist air resulting in a higher percentage cloud cover which would prevent the sun’s rays to warm the earth. The land surface was stripped bare of vegetation because of the Flood causing most of the sunlight to be deflected away. Because the land surface was so cold, any snow that fell there would not have melted quickly, but rather, it would have remained there to form hard ice cap layers.

qa.question: What is the ‘recipe’ required for an Ice Age?
qa.answer: A lot of moisture and therefore, an enormous amount of warm water. At the same time, a cold land surface would be required.

qa.question: When did the Ice Age occur?
qa.answer: The Ice Age must have commenced after the Flood and continued until the oceans cooled considerably and the climate began to stabilize.

qa.question: How long did the Ice Age last?
qa.answer: Most creation scientists believe that the Ice Age lasted for about 700 years. It took about 500 of the 700 years for the ice caps to build up and 200 of the 700 years to melt down.

qa.question: How many Ice Ages were there and how much of the earth did the ice cover?
qa.answer: These unique conditions for an Ice Age to develop occurred only once in the history of the world, so there was only one Ice Age. The ice never covered more than one third (1/3) of the earth’s surface.

qa.question: What do most scientists believe regarding the Ice Age?
qa.answer: They believe that many ice ages have occurred over a fictional period of two million years, five of them being of major significance. Considering the unique conditions required for the commencement of just a single Ice Age, this claim is quite unrealistic.

qa.question: Most people think mammoths were prehistoric animals. Does that make sense to you?
qa.answer: When the Polar regions froze, the animals in the far north, such as mammoths, were trapped and overwhelmed by the freezing cold conditions and ice. However, other familiar that were also suddenly frozen include bears, wolves, jackals, saber toothed tigers, lynx, horses, camels, goats, bison, sheep, rats, etc. These are not prehistoric, so why would the mammoth be prehistoric?

qa.question: Why is it not possible for mammoths to have lived and be frozen millions of years ago?
qa.answer: Mammoths have been discovered of which the meat was still edible! Dogs ate it and even some people. Since their remains were discovered on top of the Flood sediments, they must have frozen some time after the Flood. Radiocarbon dating has indicated the extinction of the mammoths at less than 4,000 years ago, which is of course the correct age according to the Flood events (±2,348 BC).

qa.question: Have people really seen them?
qa.answer: Rock paintings of mammoths were made by people who obviously lived with them after the Flood. How else would you draw something in such detail if you’ve never seen it before? The indigenous Evenk tribe of North-eastern Siberia has well-preserved mammoth skins in their possession. They have described in detail what the animals looked like, how they behaved, what they ate as well as how they hunted these animals themselves. During a Russian expedition in 1922, written records of living mammoths were discovered within this tribe. The most interesting was the discovery of Colonel John Blashford-Snell. He discovered two of these elephants with features similar to extinct elephants such as the mammoths in western Nepal; and he took photo’s! Look at the presentation or check out my first book.

qa.question: What happened when the Ice Age ended?
qa.answer: Many years after the Flood, the oceans cooled down again causing less evaporation, fewer clouds and less snowfall. The volcanoes were no longer as active as during the Flood and eventually all the dust and ash had settled sufficiently for the warm rays of the sun to reheat those parts of the world. The Ice Age had ended and the warmer temperatures caused sheets of ice to begin sliding southwards from the North Pole, off the continents. Scientists refer to this as the Glacial Period.

qa.question: How do we know glaciers were larger than today?
qa.answer: When these ice sheets or glaciers slowly slide down steep slopes, they grind and crush the rock material beneath and carve out U-shaped valleys while dragging the crushed rock material along over long distances. Later, after the glacier had melted, you can clearly see the grooves in the hard rock. This is how we know that there were previously much larger ice sheets present than today.

qa.question: How did people and animals distribute to other continents?
qa.answer: During the Ice Age the sea level was much lower than today because so much water had been locked into the ice cover. Consequently, for a long time, land bridges would have been available whereby people and animals could have moved to other continents. Smaller animals could also have crossed the sea on rafts consisting of pumice or floating vegetation.

qa.question: What did the animals possibly eat in the time after they disembarked from the Ark?
qa.answer: The large amounts of vegetation, including the remnants of trees, which must have been stranded en masse after the Flood would have made the growth of many types of fungi (mushrooms) possible; Seaweed; Carrion; Carcasses; Fish trapped in pools; Insect, earthworm and rodent populations would have grown explosively. Various plants already began to grow before the ark inhabitants disembarked.

qa.question: How did the plants grow again after the Flood?
qa.answer: Through vegetative propagation (where new plants grow from roots, stems or leaves, and where the normal reproductive organs such as seeds/flowers etc, are not involved). Also, seeds that are in a dormant or resting state can survive as ‘passengers’ for long periods, even when they are soaked in water (they could have survived on floating vegetation rafts). Many seeds were buried in early Flood deposits and later exposed by erosion. In addition, Noah may have taken various kinds of seed onboard as well.

qa.question: How do we know that there were already some plants when they disembarked the Ark?
qa.answer: A dove brought an olive leaf to Noah in the Ark, which clearly means that olive trees and possibly a large variety of other plants had already begun to grow even before they ventured out of the Ark

qa.question: How did the dinosaurs become extinct?
qa.answer: All the dinosaurs, except those in the Ark, were destroyed and buried during the Flood. One pair of every kind of land animal, including dinosaurs as well as birds and pterosaurs survived in Noah’s Ark, filling the earth again after the Flood. Since that time, many different animals have become extinct, not only the dinosaurs, as a constant reminder of the serious consequences of sin on Creation. After the Flood, animals and people began to fear each other, which is in harmony with Genesis 9:3 where humans were given permission to eat meat. This is why they were hunted to the point of possible extinction. As in the case of the Dodo of Mauritius, it is more than possible that dinosaurs became extinct due to human impact; especially since people saw them as such a threat.

qa.question: Read Gen 9:18-19. Where do all the people of today come from according to this verse?
qa.answer: The whole earth was populated from the three sons of Noah - Sem, Ham and Japheth (and their wives) and their descent can clearly be traced back to Adam and Eve since Adam was Noah’s great, great, great, great, great, great, great (x7) grandpa.

qa.question: How do we know that the earth is not over populated?
qa.answer: Because calculations have shown that a world population of six billion people could easily fit into a small country like England; and then each one would have about 20 square meters of space around him/her. The current (2022) world population of around 8 billions is not much more than that.

qa.question: What is exponential growth?
qa.answer: This is when a populations’ growth doubles after every subsequent population. With regard to the human population, it means that after each subsequent generation, there were more people than during the previous generation.

qa.question: What growth rate do we need to account for the number of people on earth today if it began with only eight?
qa.answer: Only 0.45% (instead of more than 1% today)

qa.question: If we use the 0.45% population growth rate, how many times would the subsequent populations, beginning with only eight people, need to double to reach the current number of people on earth?
qa.answer: Only 30 times

qa.question: Are there different human races?
qa.answer: No, there is only one human race, but their are different people (ethnic) groups)

qa.question: Read Acts 17:26-27. Are we all related to Adam and Eve?
qa.answer: Yes, Eve means ‘life’ which makes sense because Eve is the mother of all humankind. From this verse we clearly learn that every human being on earth is related to the other because it is written: “And He has made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth”.

qa.question: Why do skin color differ?
qa.answer: We all have the same skin coloring pigment responsible for our skin color, called melanin and melanin works like a kind of sunblock. The more melanin you have, the darker your skin would be and the longer it would take for you to burn in the sun. The less you have, the lighter your skin color would be and the easier or faster you would burn in the sun.

qa.question: Where do all the different languages come from?
qa.answer: It began at the Tower of Babel when God confused their languages because of their disobedience when He told them to distribute over the earth and fill it.

qa.question: How did people distribute over the earth?
qa.answer: After God confused their languages (because of their disobedience), they could not understand one another any more. The people that were able to understand one another (because they now spoke the same specific language) began to group together, and eventually moved away to places where they could live and work together without so much confusion. And so God ensured that they distributed over the earth to fill it, anyway.

qa.question: Why do people in Africa mostly have a dark skin color, while people in Europe mostly have a light skin color?
qa.answer: The people groups that understood one another distributed in all directions: Asia, North and South America, Europe, Africa and Australia. Some individuals in these groups would have had the same skin color, but there must have also been a wide variety of skin colors in each group. Groups that reached the warmer parts of Africa and Australia: Individuals with a very light skin color would have burned faster in the sun than those with darker skin, since they had less melanin to protect them from the sun. They may have contracted skin cancer, later becoming too ill to have children and eventually dying after being continually exposed to the sun. In time, mostly people with darker skin would therefore have survived in Africa and Australia since they were better adapted to the harsh climatic conditions in these areas as they had more melanin in their skin. Groups that reached the cooler, cloudier northern parts of Europe: All people need some sunshine on their skin so that they can produce Vitamin D. People with lighter skin only need a little bit of sun to do so, but people with darker skin need more sunlight since their darker skin would prevent them from absorbing much sunlight. Remember, melanin acts like a sunblock. Consequently, people with darker skins would have become very ill in these cloudy areas, because their bodies would not have been able to produce enough Vitamin D. As time went by, the darker-skinned people would have died while people with lighter skin would mostly have been able to survive in these areas with high cloud cover since they were better adapted to those climatic conditions.

qa.question: The Inuit (Eskimo’s) have brown skin, yet they live where there is not much sun. Why don’t they suffer from Vitamin D deficiency?
qa.answer: They probably have the same genetic make-up for a medium-colour skin. Yet they don’t suffer from Vitamin D deficiency since they obtain most of their Vitamin D from their diet of predominantly fish.

qa.question: Why did the confusion of languages at Babel become a stumbling block in the spreading of the Gospel?
qa.answer: Since people could not understand different languages, the Good News of the Gospel could not be spread to people who spoke other languages

qa.question: How did God solve this problem?
qa.answer: God blessed specific people in the Christian Church with the gift of speaking in tongues — without them even having to learn the specific language (See Acts 2, 10 and 19). Speaking in tongues means to have the gift to speak in a specific understandable language so that the Gospel truth can be clearly understood by all people, nations and tongues (in other words, people from differing languages). The purpose is therefore to spread the Good News of the Gospel to all people and all languages.

qa.question: Can you still remember how God described his Creation works?
qa.answer: During Creation week, GOD described His Creation six times as ‘good’; but after looking at His completed creative works at the end of Day 6, HE described it as ‘very good’.

qa.question: And what does this mean again?
qa.answer: It means that God created everything flawless, perfect and beautiful.

qa.question: Can you remember what ‘freedom of choice’ means?
qa.answer: God created mankind with the ability to choose, because true love will always give you the freedom to choose. This means that you can choose for yourself whether you want to love, serve and obey God.

qa.question: What important point should we always remember when it comes to ‘freedom of choice’?
qa.answer: With this ability to choose comes a huge responsibility, because choices always have consequences.

qa.question: Did Adam & Eve make the right choice when God gave them His first instruction?
qa.answer: No!

qa.question: What was the consequences of their wrong decision?
qa.answer: When Adam and Eve chose to be disobedient to God, they also chose the tragic consequences that would affect them as well as all of their descendants, including you and me. Those consequences include things such as pests and diseases, famine, war, hatred, suffering, pain, sadness, evil and ultimately, death.

qa.question: Many people blame God and ask how He can be a loving God when we see all these terrible things happening in the world today. Is it God’s fault?
qa.answer: Certainly not — this is the sad and tragic consequences of disobedience to God

qa.question: How is the reaction of people to God’s warning in the time of Noah similar today?
qa.answer: People in Noah’s time took absolutely no notice of the 120-year warning that God was about to bring a great destruction on the earth; and despite Noah’s continual warning while building the Ark, people ignored this serious warning and instead, they mocked and laughed at Noah every opportunity they got. That period was actually a period of grace because they had a 120-years to repent and trust in God. In this last period of grace of earth’s history, there is once again a very serious warning given in advance to everyone on earth; and that is that Jesus will soon return to Earth; and this time, HE is not only coming as the Savior of His children, but HE is also coming as the Judge of the universe to pass judgment on all the unbelievers and false Christians. [Read 2 Pet 3:10-12.] As it was in the days of Noah, there are people today who simply don’t believe that this warning is true at all, but this does not change the fact that it will happen.

qa.question: What is sin?
qa.answer: Sin is anything we think, do, or say in violation of God’s commandments.

qa.question: Where do we find those Commandments again?
qa.answer: In Exodus 20. God wrote these Commandments in stone with His own finger; and when something is written in stone, it means that it is forever. The Ten Commandments are like a mirror that shows us where we have been stained by sin.

qa.question: Is all sin equally serious?
qa.answer: Sin is sin. In God’s eyes all sins are equally serious because all sins eventually lead to eternal death. Read Romans 6:23. God wants to give us eternal life, not eternal death.

qa.question: Why does God have to punish sinners?
qa.answer: Because God is 100% love, but also 100% righteous and holy. Therefore, HE must punish the sinner because HE cannot be anything but a righteous God.

qa.question: What is the punishment for sin?
qa.answer: Eternal death

qa.question: Who will save us?
qa.answer: Jesus stands ready and willing to forgive our sins and save us from eternal death.

qa.question: How did Jesus become our Savior?
qa.answer: Even before the Creation, the heavenly Family already had a solution for this sad state of affairs. God is omniscient, which means, HE knows everything. HE created man with a free will and HE knew that they might choose to be disobedient; and if that were to happen, there had to be a plan to save mankind from sin and its deadly consequence. The plan was that ONE of the Persons of the Godhead would pay the penalty for our sin. That person was Jesus!

qa.question: Wasn’t it cruel of God the Father to allow His Son to pay the penalty that we deserve?
qa.answer: Read Joh 10:17-18 & Phil 2:6-8. In these verses we clearly see that Jesus, the Son Himself voluntarily offered to lay down His life because HE loves the Father and us infinitely! No-one forced Him to do so and the Son did not make any decision on His own, but always according to His Father’s will. The plan of salvation was therefore determined by the Godhead in unity.

qa.question: What is the Good News of the Gospel?
qa.answer: The Good News of the Gospel is that Jesus has already paid the penalty for our sins. HE became the perfect sacrifice by dying on the cross. But more importantly, HE rose from the grave to be the Savior of every person who chooses to accept His free gift of salvation.

qa.question: What does it mean when I accept this free gift? Can I still continue doing the same
qa.answer: wrong things as before? Certainly not! By accepting this free gift, we choose to live our lives according to the example Jesus gave us. We cannot do that in our own strength, but only through the strength of Jesus, our Savior.

qa.question: What beautiful promise has God given to us if we made this choice?
qa.answer: Jesus promised that every person who made this choice would live with Him in the Heavenly Paradise - forever! Our Creator will recreate us physically by clothing us with immortality at His Second Coming. Never again will there be sin or death. Nobody will ever be afraid, sad or alone again. Read Romans 6:23

qa.question: Could there perhaps be someone else or another way that could save us?
qa.answer: No! Read John 10:9 and 14:6

qa.question: What can we do to be saved?
qa.answer: This is the most important question you will ever ask yourself. • We must confess our sin. (We should admit to God that we have sinned — ourselves) • We must be sincerely sorry and repent. ‘Repent’ means to turn away from sin. Turn to God. Tell Him how sorry you are for what you have done and stop doing it — turn away from it. • We must ask Jesus to cleanse us from our sin and to be our personal Savior. • We must honestly try not to sin again. If we apologize while already planning in our hearts to sin again, then we are not sincerely sorry and God cannot forgive us. Remember, God always looks at what is in our hearts (our minds). We cannot hide anything from Him, not even our thoughts. Therefore, when we confess and repent, we need to truly mean what we say. As hard as we try, we all seem to stumble and sin again every now and then. When this happens, happens, confess it to God immediately and ask for His forgiveness. Don’t wait until tonight when you go to bed. Don’t become discouraged! We simply cannot conquer sin in our own strength. We need Jesus every second of every day so that we, through His strength, can make the right choices. • Get to know God. Study His Word, the Bible. Pray and talk to God about everything in your life and as often as possible. We can do that in our thoughts or out loud. HE is interested in every little detail of our lives and HE wants us to share our thoughts, worries, hopes and dreams with Him. You can even write letters to Him if you like — as in a journal. We need to follow the instructions that He gave to us in His Word, The Bible, so that HE can protect us against THE enemy of mankind — satan. HE cannot do that if we choose to remove ourselves from His protective umbrella • And remember, even if you were the only person on earth, Jesus still would have laid down His life to save you. He loves us more than we can ever truly understand.
